rule: มัน splits three ways. The tuber plant (1) takes the named yams and potatoes and their roots. Fat (2) takes every compound whose มัน is the substance itself: a cut of fat, oil to fry in, the oily secretion of musth, and anything named after a blob or colour of fat. Rich taste (3) takes food whose point is the coconut-cream richness. The pronoun (5) heads nothing here.

notes.text:
**Rule.** มัน splits three ways. The tuber (1) takes the named yams and
potatoes and their roots. Fat (2) takes every compound where มัน is the
substance itself: a cut of fat, oil to fry in, the oily discharge of musth, and
anything named after a blob or a colour of fat. Rich taste (3) takes food whose
point is coconut-cream richness. No compound here is built on the pronoun (5).

1  มันเทศ, มันฝรั่ง, หัวมัน                                         3
    2  มันเปลว, มันแข็ง, ทอดมัน, ตกมัน, กลัดมัน, มันปู, สีน้ำมัน, ฟองมัน  8
    3  ข้าวมัน                                                        1

**Unsure.**
* **ฟองมัน → 2.** This is the ๏ sign. I read it as a fat globule, the round
  bead of fat that floats on broth. Nothing on disk explains the name, and
  thai-full gives only ฟอง + มัน.
* **กลัดมัน → 2.** I filed it next to ตกมัน as the swollen, rutting state.
  It could go under 6, "absorbed". thai-full has no etymology for it.
* **สีน้ำมัน → 2.** The parts are mis-split as สีน้ำ + มัน. The word is
  really สี + น้ำมัน. The มัน inside it is still fat.
* **กระมัน is left unfiled.** It is a fish name, glossed only as กระโห้, and
  has no etymology. None of มัน's senses accounts for it.
